A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hugging Carbon study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original analysis of Hugging Face training emissions, fitted regressions, disclosed-emissions validation, Monte Carlo uncertainty decomposition, and pseudo-missingness experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical analyses and reports revised corpus counts and emissions estimates.

M1.justification: Appendix C explicitly states that v2 updates the experiments by applying a general 1.5× MoE overhead correction; v1 discussed a possible 1.4–2.0× correction without specifying this applied choice. The underlying tiered accounting framework and regression models remain intact.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 and Figure 5 remove projections for the broader populations with over 100 and over 1,000 downloads, retaining only the over-5,000-download population. The principal Hugging Face domains and training-emissions task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a new competing emissions estimator. Table 2 retains the same model and model-series comparisons against disclosed emissions; changes to related-work names and citations do not alter evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: Appendix A revises the retained corpus from 5,234 to 5,227 models, with deduplication exclusions increasing from 1,404 to 1,411. The August 2025 snapshot, main download threshold, 292-model validation, error metrics, and Appendix H masking procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The disclosed-emissions error analysis, Appendix G uncertainty decomposition, and Appendix H pseudo-missingness tests retain their designs and analytical questions. The MoE correction is not accompanied by a new ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same regression standard-error reporting, first-order uncertainty propagation, tier uncertainty assumptions, and 1,000 Monte Carlo samples per factor. The revised aggregate uncertainty value is a result update, not a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Aggregate emissions change from approximately 58,000 ±20,000 to 60,000 ±24,000 tCO2e. Table 1 revises several totals and ATCI values; Table 2 changes OLMoE-1B-7B-0924 from 20 to 30 tCO2e against an unchanged disclosure of 18. The retained 2035 projection changes from approximately 99,000 to 94,000 tCO2e. These are revised estimates with updated accounting and sampling, not demonstrated accuracy gains; the principal trends and validation tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The emissions and ATCI definitions, architecture-specific FLOPs formulas, regression equations, and uncertainty derivations are retained. The main uncertainty equation is renumbered from (7) to (6); the empirical MoE multiplier does not introduce a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the assertion that Hugging Face well represents the broader open-source community and removes the 'audit-ready' characterization. The conclusion replaces the medium-sized-country-for-several-weeks comparison with annual resident and passenger-car equivalents. The central accounting and ATCI contributions remain.

C2.justification: The interpretation of footprint scale is refined: Figure 1 replaces EU homes' annual energy use with EU residents' annual greenhouse-gas footprints, and the conclusion adopts corresponding person/car comparisons. The hardware and modality explanations and limitations concerning proprietary models, inference, and lifecycle emissions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data availability statement and repository link. Section 3.3 and Appendix E.3 specify same-category mean-emissions imputation when parameter counts are unavailable, while Table 2 identifies the variants included in its Llama 2 and CodeLlama totals. These are added documentation; they do not independently establish when the fallback was implemented.

R1.justification: The car-equivalence reference changes from Tiegte et al. (2021) to the European Environment Agency (2024). Section 2 changes 'industry-scale' positioning to 'platform-scale' and softens the categorical exclusion of runtime-monitoring tools. Several other references receive publication-metadata updates rather than representing newly cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory framework description are revised, terminology and headings are polished, and publication and bibliographic text are updated. The section order and Appendix A–H organization remain intact, with limited explanatory additions.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 are redrawn with revised axes and labels; Figure 5 becomes a single forecast curve and moves to page 8. Figure 3 changes column placement, Figure 1 labels are revised, and Table 2 gains an explanatory caption. Most appendix displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through an explicit applied MoE correction, clearer fallback documentation, and code/data access information. Its resident-footprint comparison also better matches the cited per-capita measure than v1's household comparison. These are limited gains: forecast coverage narrows, and unchanged validation in Tables 3 and 11 provides no evidence of improved estimation accuracy.
